name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q01 - Genetic and species levels of biodiversity

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: The medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria shows genetic variation in the potency and concentration of reserpine.

Statement II: India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice and 1,000 varieties of mango.

Statement III: The Eastern Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Western Ghats.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the proposition on Rauwolfia vomitoria. Populations of this medicinal plant growing in different Himalayan ranges exhibit genetic variation in the concentration and pharmacological potency of the active alkaloid reserpine. This proposition is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluate the proposition on crop genetic diversity in India. Documented agricultural records confirm that India possesses more than 50,000 genetically distinct strains of rice and approximately 1,000 horticultural varieties of mango. This proposition is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluate the proposition on amphibian diversity across the Ghats. The Western Ghats, with their dense tropical rainforests and high precipitation, harbour significantly greater amphibian species richness than the drier Eastern Ghats. This proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding reserpine variation in Rauwolfia and Indian crop varieties are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q02 - Recorded species proportions across animal taxa

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Plants comprise more than 70 per cent of all recorded living species on Earth.

Statement II: Animals comprise more than 70 per cent of all recorded living species on Earth.

Statement III: Among animals, insects constitute the most species-rich group, representing more than 70 per cent of the total.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the proposition regarding plant species representation. Globally catalogued inventories establish that plants (including algae, fungi, bryophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms) comprise no more than 22 per cent of described species. Claiming they comprise more than 70 per cent is false.

Step 2: Evaluate the proposition regarding animal species representation. Recorded taxonomic surveys confirm that animals account for more than 70 per cent of all documented species, validating this claim.

Step 3: Evaluate the proposition regarding insect dominance. Within the animal kingdom, insects are the single most diverse class, making up more than 70 per cent of all recorded animals (7 out of every 10 animals are insects), validating this claim.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding animal dominance over 70 per cent and insect richness among animals are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q03 - Comparative species richness of major taxa

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: The number of fungi species in the world exceeds the combined total of the species of fishes, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals.

Statement II: Prokaryotic species diversity is completely catalogued because all bacteria are culturable on synthetic laboratory media.

Statement III: Among vertebrates, fishes account for nearly half of all described species.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the proposition on fungi species richness. The textbook explicitly highlights that global species of fungi outnumber the combined total of all four major vertebrate classes (fishes, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals). This proposition is verified and accurate.

Step 2: Evaluate the proposition on microbial diversity and culturability. Most natural prokaryotic species cannot be cultured under laboratory conditions, and conventional taxonomy cannot reliably delineate them. Claiming that prokaryotes are completely catalogued and easily cultured is false.

Step 3: Evaluate the proposition on vertebrate taxa proportions. In global biodiversity representations, fishes constitute approximately 50 per cent of all vertebrate species, validating this proposition.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding fungal species richness and fish dominance among vertebrates are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q04 - Biodiversity metrics and megadiversity in India

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: India accounts for 2.4 per cent of the world's land area.

Statement II: India's share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent.

Statement III: India is recognized as one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the geographic area of India. India occupies 2.4 per cent of the total terrestrial land surface of the planet, which is an accurate geographical figure.

Step 2: Evaluate the biodiversity share of India. Despite having only 2.4 per cent of global land, India contributes 8.1 per cent to global species diversity, which is an accurate biological figure.

Step 3: Evaluate India's status among global biodiversity centers. This disproportionately high species richness places India among the 12 elite mega diversity countries globally, confirming this status.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

All three statements are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q05 - Latitudinal bird species richness gradients globally

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Colombia, located near the equator, has nearly 1,400 species of birds.

Statement II: Greenland, located at 71° N, possesses only about 56 species of birds.

Statement III: New York, located at 41° N, has more than 1,200 species of birds.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the avian richness of Colombia. Colombia, situated in equatorial tropical latitudes, houses nearly 1,400 documented bird species, validating this claim.

Step 2: Evaluate the avian richness of Greenland. High-latitude arctic Greenland (71° N) supports only 56 bird species due to extreme cold and reduced energy availability, validating this claim.

Step 3: Evaluate the avian richness of New York. Temperate New York (41° N) harbours 105 bird species, not more than 1,200 (the figure of > 1,200 corresponds to India). Therefore, this claim is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding Colombia and Greenland bird counts are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q06 - Hypotheses explaining higher tropical species richness

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Tropical latitudes were subjected to frequent destructive glaciations throughout geological history.

Statement II: Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively constant, and predictable, promoting niche specialisation.

Statement III: Greater availability of solar energy in the tropics contributes to higher primary productivity and indirectly to higher diversity.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the glaciations hypothesis. Temperate zones underwent recurrent Pleistocene glaciations, while tropical latitudes remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, providing uninterrupted evolutionary speciation time. Stating that tropics experienced frequent glaciations is false.

Step 2: Evaluate environmental seasonality in the tropics. Tropical climates are less seasonal and more predictable, allowing fine resource partitioning and specialized ecological niches. This premise is fully validated.

Step 3: Evaluate solar insolation and primary productivity. Year-round abundant solar energy drives high primary production, supporting intricate food webs and higher species richness. This premise is fully validated.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding niche specialisation in constant environments and solar energy productivity are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q07 - Species area regression coefficients and scaling

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: The regression slope \(Z\) for regional species-area curves consistently lies in the range of 0.1 to 0.2.

Statement II: When species-area relationships are analysed across entire continents, the regression slope becomes much flatter, falling below 0.05.

Statement III: For frugivorous birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents, the regression slope \(Z\) is 1.15.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate regional regression slopes. Across compact geographical regions (such as plants in Britain or birds in California), ecologists consistently observe regression slopes \(Z\) between 0.1 and 0.2. This proposition is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluate continental-scale regression slopes. When scaling up to entire continents, the curve becomes significantly steeper—not flatter—with \(Z\) values in the range of 0.6 to 1.2. Hence, claiming the slope drops below 0.05 is false.

Step 3: Evaluate the specific continental survey of frugivorous vertebrates. In tropical forests across different continents, the slope \(Z\) for fruit-eating birds and mammals is empirically established to be 1.15. This proposition is accurate.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding regional slope values (0.1 to 0.2) and continental frugivorous vertebrate slope (1.15) are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q08 - Community stability and rivet popper hypothesis

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: A stable community should not show too much variation in productivity from year to year.

Statement II: David Tilman showed that plots with more species exhibited less year-to-year variation in total biomass.

Statement III: In Paul Ehrlich's rivet popper hypothesis, loss of rivets on the wings represents loss of key species driving major ecosystem functions.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the defined criteria of biological community stability. Ecologists agree that a stable community must display low annual variation in productivity, resilience to disturbances, and resistance to invasive alien species. This premise is completely verified.

Step 2: Evaluate David Tilman's empirical ecosystem experiments. Tilman's long-term outdoor plots demonstrated that species-rich communities showed significantly less year-to-year biomass fluctuation and higher overall productivity. This premise is completely verified.

Step 3: Evaluate the keystone analogy in the rivet popper model. Ehrlich compared ecosystem functioning to an airplane, where rivets on the wings correspond to keystone species driving major processes; their removal directly endangers ecological safety. This premise is completely verified.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

All three statements are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q09 - Documented recent extinctions and geographic localities

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: The dodo was a flightless bird native to Mauritius that became extinct in recent history.

Statement II: The thylacine was a carnivorous marsupial native to Australia that is now extinct.

Statement III: The quagga was a marine mammal native to Russia that became extinct due to over-exploitation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Verify the origin and extinction of the dodo. The dodo (Raphus cucullatus) was an endemic flightless bird of Mauritius that suffered extinction after human arrival, confirming this statement.

Step 2: Verify the origin and extinction of the thylacine. The thylacine (Tasmanian wolf) was a carnivorous marsupial endemic to Australia that became extinct in the 20th century, confirming this statement.

Step 3: Verify the identity and origin of the quagga. The quagga was a zebra subspecies native to Africa, whereas Steller's sea cow was the marine mammal native to Russia. Stating that the quagga was a marine mammal from Russia is factually erroneous.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding the dodo of Mauritius and the thylacine of Australia are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q10 - Extinction rates and vulnerable taxonomic groups

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Current species extinction rates are estimated to be 100 to 1,000 times slower than background pre-human rates.

Statement II: Extinctions across taxa are not random, with amphibians appearing to be particularly vulnerable to extinction.

Statement III: Presently, 32 per cent of all amphibian species and 31 per cent of all gymnosperm species worldwide face the threat of extinction.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the rate of the ongoing Sixth Extinction. Human activities have accelerated extinction rates to 100 to 1,000 times faster—not slower—than background pre-human rates. Hence, this statement is false.

Step 2: Evaluate vulnerability patterns across taxonomic classes. Documented extinction data demonstrates that extinction risks are non-random across taxa and that amphibians display acute vulnerability worldwide. Hence, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluate the exact percentage of threatened groups. According to the Red List, 32 per cent of amphibians and 31 per cent of gymnosperms face extinction threat worldwide, confirming these statistics.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding non-random vulnerability of amphibians and the 32 per cent threat level are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q11 - Alien species invasions in varied biomes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: The introduction of the Nile perch into Lake Victoria led to the extinction of more than 200 species of native cichlid fish.

Statement II: The illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture poses no threat to indigenous catfishes in Indian rivers.

Statement III: Carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana, and water hyacinth (Eichhornia) are invasive alien weeds causing severe environmental damage in India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Nile perch invasion in Lake Victoria. Introducing the predatory Nile perch precipitated the catastrophic extinction of over 200 species of endemic cichlids in Lake Victoria. This proposition is verified and accurate.

Step 2: Evaluate the introduction of Clarias gariepinus in Indian rivers. The illegal aquaculture introduction of the exotic African catfish poses a direct, grave predatory and competitive threat to indigenous catfish species, contrary to the claim of no threat. Hence, this proposition is false.

Step 3: Evaluate invasive alien plants in India. Parthenium, Lantana, and Eichhornia are classic noxious invasive weed species that aggressively overrun native vegetation and waterways across India. This proposition is accurate.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding the Nile perch in Lake Victoria and invasive weeds in India are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q12 - Categories of utilitarian arguments for conservation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity emphasize direct economic benefits such as food, firewood, fiber, and pharmaceuticals.

Statement II: More than 25 per cent of all prescription drugs sold worldwide are derived from plant sources.

Statement III: Bioprospecting refers to exploring molecular, genetic, and species-level diversity for products of economic importance.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the scope of narrowly utilitarian arguments. Narrowly utilitarian motivations focus on tangible, direct commercial and subsistence goods obtained from biodiversity, including cereals, fruits, timber, resins, tannins, and medicines. This definition is completely accurate.

Step 2: Evaluate pharmaceutical dependence on botanical biodiversity. Global pharmacopeia data confirms that over 25 per cent of modern prescription drugs are directly derived from plant biochemicals, and 25,000 plant species serve traditional medicine, making this claim accurate.

Step 3: Evaluate the formal definition of bioprospecting. Bioprospecting is defined as the systematic search for valuable chemical compounds, genes, and biomolecules from nature for economic application, validating this definition.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

All three statements are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q13 - Biodiversity hotspots criteria and Indian coverage

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Biodiversity hotspots are regions characterized by exceptionally high species richness and high endemism.

Statement II: Initially 25 biodiversity hotspots were identified globally, but subsequently nine more were added, bringing the total to 34.

Statement III: Biodiversity hotspots cover more than 15 per cent of the Earth's terrestrial land area.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the diagnostic criteria of biodiversity hotspots. Hotspots are officially defined by exceptional species richness, high levels of endemism, and high rates of habitat degradation. This statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluate the historical enumeration of global hotspots. Conservationists initially designated 25 hotspots, later adding 9 more to arrive at the current total of 34 global hotspots. This statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluate total surface land area occupied by hotspots. Collectively, all 34 global hotspots cover less than 2 per cent of the Earth's terrestrial land area, not more than 15 per cent. Hence, this statement is false.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding hotspot definition and their global number (34) are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q14 - Sacred groves and ex situ conservation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Sacred groves in India are managed strictly as ex situ conservation facilities inside zoological parks.

Statement II: Sacred groves are found in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, the Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan, and the Western Ghats.

Statement III: Modern ex situ conservation includes cryopreservation of gametes in fertile condition, in vitro fertilisation, and seed banks.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the classification of sacred groves. Sacred groves represent forest tracts set aside through cultural and religious traditions where communities venerate and protect all trees and wildlife in their natural habitat; this is a form of in situ (on-site) conservation, not ex situ. Hence, the initial statement is false.

Step 2: Verify geographic locations of sacred groves in India. Well-known sacred groves are located in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya, the Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan, the Western Ghats of Karnataka and Maharashtra, and the Sarguja, Chanda, and Bastar areas. This statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluate modern techniques of ex situ conservation. Beyond physical animal enclosures, advanced off-site conservation utilizes cryopreservation of gametes at ultra-low temperatures, in vitro fertilisation of eggs, and long-term storage in seed banks. This statement is accurate.

Step 4: Conclude the correct combination.

Only the statements regarding the geographic distribution of sacred groves and advanced ex situ techniques are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III
